minutes.headline: EDC agreed to ask the town for a small budget for next year's Town Official Meet and Greet and to seek a workshop with the land use director on small-business hurdles.
minutes.summary: The Economic Development Committee, meeting by Zoom, reviewed the fall Town Official Meet and Greet and how to get more town officials and employees to attend. Members discussed asking the town for a modest budget so the event no longer depends on donated venue, food and sponsor funds. They also discussed 2025 goals: easing small-business zoning hurdles, a crosswalk, banners, and the May vendor fair. No formal vote other than adjournment was taken.

budget_items.what_was_said: The member who ran it said spending was close to a stated amount, not counting donated venue and food.
Members discussed asking for a modest amount so the organizer would not have to solicit sponsorships or handle sponsor funds.
The requested amount would cover out-of-pocket items such as the DJ that organizers had paid themselves.

decisions.decision: Chair Kathy Clark will email the land use director first (then the town manager) to request town budget funding for next year's Meet and Greet, with a figure around 2,500 discussed.
Members will document all Meet and Greet procedures and contacts in a shared Google Drive for continuity.
Plan to invite town committees and employees to the next Meet and Greet starting in August, and ask the select board to have the town manager direct department heads to attend.
Seek a workshop or afternoon EDC meeting with the land use director on small-business zoning hurdles, possibly as next month's meeting; the chair will email members for availability.
Members will ask the Municipal Building Committee to incorporate a crosswalk in its design so a plan can be submitted to MassDOT.
EDC will seek a table at the May vendor fair hosted by Parks in collaboration with the LBA.
